newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat firms on spot demand, ignores rebates.
newsitem.headline: French wheat firms on spot demand, ignores rebates.

text.p: French wheat prices for prompt delivery firmed on Friday on fresh buying, dealers said.
But the market largely ignored news the European Commission had raised its wheat export subsidy to 22.35 Ecus, mostly because the rebate was not as much as some operators had expected.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 845 francs per tonne for November delivery and at 835 francs for December delivery, both up five francs on Thursday.
Operators anxious to cover cargoes loading at Rouen were having difficulty securing prompt grain, dealers said.
Less wheat is available in port silos than was initially expected.
With the sugar beet harvest now in full swing, producers are finding it hard to get hold of trucks to transport grain.
In France traders had bid to export 706,500 tonnes of soft wheat at rebates ranging from 20.47 to 28.89 Ecus through the EU grain tender system on Thursday.
But the EU awarded only 350,500 tonnes of wheat at a 22.35 Ecus per tonne rebate.
One dealer calculated that if the EU had awarded only an extra 0.12 Ecus, it would have been able to export 400,000 tonnes of wheat.
Volume on MATIF wheat futures was a modest 60 lots with the February 1997 expiry quoted at 864 francs, up two francs on Thursday.
